pages.text: "From here, I'll see Dad's boat first!" From the bridge railing in spring, Pongi looked down at the canal. Today Dad was coming back from the market by boat. Pongi wanted to be the first to welcome him.
But Dad's boat wasn't on the canal. Only calm water. Pongi rested her paws on the railing and twisted from side to side. "When is he coming...?" Her brother sat beside her with his shell.
"I'm bored! Still not here?" Pongi stamped her feet. The canal looked just the same, and only the reeds on the bank swayed. Pongi pouted to one side.
Mom, wearing her headscarf, winked. "Shall we play count-the-boats, Pongi? Boats passing by, one, two!" "What's count-the-boats?" Pongi lifted her head from the railing.
"We count the boats that pass until Dad's boat comes." A boat tooted and went under the bridge. It was loaded with bread. "One!" counted Mom.
Now it was Pongi's turn. A boat came from the left. "Two! That's a reed boat!" She pointed. On the boring canal, more and more things appeared to look at.
Next was her brother's turn. Another boat went under the bridge. He raised his shell. "Three!" They took turns counting. Waiting wasn't boring at all.
Ha, ha, ha! All three laughed on the bridge. Pongi thumped her tail on the bridge floor. Being bored had turned into a game.
Pongi rested her chin on the railing and sang, "One, count the passing boats! Two, guess what kind of boat! Three, take turns counting!" "Let's do it again next time we wait!" she said.
A boat appeared at the end of the canal. Dad's boat! Mom hugged Pongi tight. "You turned being bored into a game!" Counting can make waiting a game too. Pongi called, "Boats passing by, one, two!"
